POIIcons.Heading: POI Icons
POIIcons.FullColourNote: Off (default): icons tint to their layer's colour. On: icons render in their own colours or, for uploads, the original image.

HorizonLength.Heading: Horizon Length
HorizonLength.DescFar: Full-length horizon — more dragging to scan the whole view.
HorizonLength.DescMedium: Balanced — a middle ground between range and reach.
HorizonLength.DescClose: Short horizon — reach any point with minimal dragging.

Docking.Heading: Docking
Docking.FreeDockNote: When docked, drag the small handle above the strip to move it anywhere on your own screen instead of the auto-centred position. This is per-browser — it isn't shared with other players.

LayersInfo.Heading: Custom Layer Images
LayersInfo.Body1: Recommended: a wide, short PNG (transparent background) drawn as a horizon silhouette — around 2400×400px to 3600×600px, roughly 6:1 wide. It's stretched to fill the layer's height and tiled sideways, so keep the important shapes clear of the very top/bottom edges.
LayersInfo.Body2: Seamless tiling — when the image's left and right edges don't already line up, turn on Seamless mirror tiling next to the upload (on by default). It mirrors the image and tiles [image][flipped copy] alternately — that guarantees a perfect, jump-free loop for any image, at the cost of every other tile appearing mirrored.
LayersInfo.Body3: Prefer a true unbroken loop with no mirroring? Author the source image so its leftmost and rightmost columns already match, then turn tiling off.
LayersInfo.Body4: Solid base — layers can be dragged vertically, which opens a gap beneath artwork that doesn't already reach the bottom edge. For best results, draw your image with a flat, solid-colour base near the bottom (like the bundled Forest presets). If you don't, the module will only fill the exact gap your drag creates, straight down from wherever your art already stops — it won't guess a shape for you, so any hole left by incomplete artwork is yours to fix in the source image.
